description: [Daba Finance] Wave Côte d'Ivoire has joined the PI-SPI instant payment network, developed by the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO). The mobile money operator is now listed among the authorized participants as of September 30, 2026, after having been absent from the list on July 31, 2026. This integration marks a significant expansion of the system in Côte d'Ivoire and throughout the UEMOA. Wave has also been authorized to join the platform in Senegal.
title: Africa: Wave Joins the BCEAC's PI-SPI Instant Payment Network

description: [Daba Finance] Five35 Ventures has completed its first portfolio exit, generating a 3.5x multiple on its investment in Ghanaian agritech company Complete Farmer.
title: Africa: Five35 Ventures Posts 3.5x Return in First Portfolio Exit

description: [Daba Finance] African tech startups collectively secured $582,808,000 in funding during the third quarter of 2026. This significant capital injection was distributed among 58 different startups across the continent. The period from July to September 2026 emerged as the most successful quarter of the year so far for the African tech ecosystem, indicating a potential strengthening of investor interest.
title: Africa: African Tech Startups Secure $583 Million in Q3 Funding

description: [This Day] Former Super Eagles captain, William Troost-Ekong has identified the reason behind Nigeria's topsy-turvy start to their AFCON 2027 qualifiers.
title: Africa: Papering Over the Cracks - Troost-Ekong Exposes Nigeria's Deep-Rooted Issues Amid Afcon Qualifier Struggles

description: [This Day] Jani Ibrahim's career has followed an unusual arc: engineer first, industrialist second, institution builder last, each stage quietly funding the next. In September, that arc reached West Africa, when he was elected President of the Federation of West African Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FEWACCI).
title: Africa: Jani Ibrahim's Rise to West Africa's Business Frontline

description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Billionaire industrialist Aliko Dangote has called for faster industrialisation across Africa, saying the continent must create jobs and economic opportunities to absorb its growing young population.
title: Africa: Aliko Dangote Says Industrialisation Key to Creating Jobs for Africa's Youth

description: [Africa CDC] Accra, Ghana -- The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) is supporting Ghana to strengthen its Public Health Emergency Operations Centres (PHEOCs), which coordinate information, expertise and resources during health emergencies.
title: Africa: Ghana Steps Up Emergency Preparedness With Africa CDC Support

description: [IPS] Suva, Fiji &amp; Srinagar, India -- Extreme heat is increasingly threatening pregnant women and newborn babies around the world, with almost all maternal health professionals surveyed across five continents saying they have cared for women or infants whose health was affected by high temperatures.
title: Africa: Climate Change Is Becoming a Pregnancy Hazard Worldwide, Survey Finds

description: [Shabelle] Alamein, Egypt -- Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud on Sunday called on African and international investors to explore investment opportunities in Somalia, saying the country was rebuilding its economy and was open to business.
title: Africa: Somali President Pitches Investment Opportunities At Alamein-Africa Forum

description: [Daily Trust] |The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the African Union (AU), and other key regional blocs have signed a landmark Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to streamline the deployment of the African Standby Force (ASF).
title: Africa: Ecowas, AU, Regional Blocs Sign Pact On African Standby Force Deployment

description: [UN News] Rotting food waste is causing up to 10 per cent of total global greenhouse gas emissions - five times more than the entire aviation sector, the UN's environment agency warned this week.
title: Africa: Rotting Food Waste Emits 5 Times More Greenhouse Gases Than Planes

description: [The Conversation Africa] The new Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) has already generated an important debate. Some analysts have portrayed it as a rival to the three established global rating agencies - Fitch, Moody's and S&amp;P Global. Others have questioned whether Africa needs another rating agency at all.
title: Africa: Africa's New Credit Agency - Why It's About a Lot More Than Just Ratings

description: [The Conversation Africa] The formal launch of the Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) has required considerable institutional commitment. It brings to fruition an effort that has been almost a decade in the making.
title: Africa: Africa's New Credit Agency - Why It's Needed

description: [RFI] Thousands of years ago, farmers in West Africa took a wild ancestor of rice and turned it into a crop of their own. But it was difficult to harvest and, over time, globally dominant Asian rice pushed it aside. Yet African rice survived in some of the region's harshest growing conditions, coping with drought, deep water, poor soil, pests and punishing heat. Now, researchers in China may have found a way to make its hard-won traits easier for breeders to harness.
title: Africa: The Ancient African Rice That Could Help Farmers Grapple With Climate Change

description: [African Arguments] When one Black South African journalist decided to leave the profession after only four years, she did not walk away because she had stopped believing in journalism: 'I mourned because I knew I could have done so much in that space.'
title: Africa: African Newsrooms Can No Longer Delay Creating the Conditions for Women to Stay

description: [African Arguments] In June 2024, a ransomware attack on South Africa's National Health Laboratory Service rendered patient records inaccessible, disrupted diagnostics and forced hospitals to cancel surgeries. The incident was a stark reminder that when essential services become digital, attacks on their underlying systems can quickly become disruptions to everyday life. It was not simply a cybersecurity incident affecting an IT network; it affected health institutions' ability to deliver services.
title: Africa: Cybersecurity Is the Infrastructure Africa Is Forgetting to Build

description: [UN News] Getting aid to people in the world's most neglected emergencies takes more than money. It takes open roads, open borders and leaders willing to help it reach those in dire need.
title: Africa: 'Money Alone Won't Get Us There' - UN Steps Up Aid for 12 Forgotten Crises
